evidence.quote:
**Detect:** After stripping frontmatter and ignoring fenced blocks, the resource has at least one anchored citer, and either (a) the leading H1 carries substantial framing (roughly 100+ characters of body before the first `##`) whose only reachable anchor spans the whole file, or (b) prose sits before any heading. Mechanical: measure prose before the first `##` against the span of the leading H1 and against every `##` span. A section-scoped `get_resource` returns only the matched heading's span, so that framing is silently absent for every section consumer.

**Do not flag:** Orientation-only framing a section consumer does not need (record the verdict). Single-section resources with no anchored citers. Framing already under a named `##` that citers can request. Whole-resource citations where the consumer loads the full file (`whole-resource-for-one-section` Do-not-flag carve-outs).

**Fix:** Classify the framing — delete when it duplicates the citing technique; mint a `##` section (or move the obligation into the technique) when it is operative and unique; leave when it is orientation only. Cross-section deixis becomes an anchored link. See [A Resource Splits for Section Delivery](./design-principles.md#44-a-resource-splits-for-section-delivery) and [Cite Resources at Section Grain](./design-principles.md#32-cite-resources-at-section-grain). Related: `whole-resource-for-one-section`.

A multi-part resource splits into per-category sections, each holding the fragment for one category, with the whole-document skeleton in its own section. Shared fragments — scales, mappings, reference tables — sit in one shared section. Operative framing, shared keys, and obligations a section reader needs live under a `##` heading an anchor can deliver. The consumer fetches the section it renders.

findings.problem: A roughly 100-character leading-body threshold can miss a short operative constraint. Moving framing under a new heading makes it addressable but does not itself deliver it to existing section consumers; the Fix needs to close that dependency.
findings.witness: An H1 introduction says only "Counts include retries." before the first H2. A consumer loads an H2 table and computes counts. The missing sentence is operative and short, so the substantial-framing heuristic may miss it. Adding an H2 General Rules without changing the consumer still leaves the same missing rule.
findings.proposed_fix: Detect: "For each section-delivered resource, identify operative facts outside the delivered sections that the consumer needs. Flag any missing fact regardless of length; length may prioritize inspection but cannot decide applicability." Fix: "Move unique operative framing to an addressable section and update every dependent consumer to receive it, or place the fact within the consumed section. Verify the actual section delivery contains the needed obligation."

observing_check.method: Apply the quoted criteria to the two constructed cases; these are canon-quality witnesses, not corpus-conformance findings.
observing_check.positive: Flag the short retries-counting rule when a table consumer does not receive it; adding an unrequested heading alone does not close the finding.
observing_check.negative: Do not flag a long orientation paragraph no section consumer needs, or a shared obligation explicitly loaded alongside each dependent section.
